  [BUG] Small timeout gets treated like blocking #11732New issueCopy linkNew issueCopy linkClosedClosed[BUG] Small timeout gets treated like blocking#11732Copy linkLabelsstate:to-be-closedrequesting the core team to close the issuerequesting the core team to close the issueDescriptionjimsnabopened on Jan 17, 2023Issue body actionsDescribe the bug
A command that has a small timeout, like 1 millisecond, gets treated like 0 - which is infinitely blocking and very different than expected.
To reproduce
> BLMOVE k1 k2 left right 0.002
(nil)
> BLMOVE k1 k2 left right 0.001
... blocks indefinitely

Expected behavior
If non-zero timeout is specified, the command should not infinitely block.

The very idea of a negative timeout is weird, and there's no intuitive way to interpret it imo. part.text:
That unit file doesn't exist in this tree; `unit/type/string` is the relevant suite and fully passes. 

**Summary of the fix** (`src/t_string.c:502`, `getrangeCommand`, used by both `GETRANGE` and `SUBSTR`): the old code clamped a negative `end` to 0 after conversion, so when `end <= -strlen` and `start` clamped to the same index (e.g. `substr key 0 -500`), the range `start == end` wrongly returned the first character. Now negative indexes are converted first, and the reply is empty whenever the range falls out of bounds (`end < 0`, `start >= strlen`, `start > end`, or empty string) — matching Tcl-style range semantics. `unit/type/string` (all GETRANGE/SUBSTR tests, including the new negative-index cases) passes, and the issue's reproduction now returns an empty string.
